# extras


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

These helpers extend `fastcolab.core`. Two call Colab’s older `/tun/m/`
endpoints for account balances and browser links absent from `v1beta`.
The rest wire up SSH via `jupyasyncclient.ssh`, shell commands, hardware
checks, directory syncing, remote notebooks, and ephemeral scripts.

## Live compute unit balance and burn rate

Colab’s `v1beta` REST API returns only your subscription tier
(`SUBSCRIPTION_TIER_PRO_PLUS`). Live credit balance and hourly burn rate
live on Colab’s older tunnel backend at
`https://colab.research.google.com/tun/m/ccu-info`. Every response
starts with `)]}'\n` to prevent cross-site script inclusion.
[`_tunnel_get`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/fastcolab/extras.html#_tunnel_get)
refreshes stale credentials, sends `authuser=0` and
`X-Colab-Client-Agent`, and strips that prefix.

[`ColabUsage`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/fastcolab/extras.html#colabusage)
wraps the raw `ccu-info` fields in short snake_case properties and
renders a compact summary in notebooks.
[`Colab.usage`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/fastcolab/extras.html#colab.usage)
calls `/tun/m/ccu-info` using the credentials already attached to
[`Colab`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/fastcolab/core.html#colab).

Connect to Colab and check the live balance before starting a server.
`gclientid`’s `colab` preset already grants `userinfo.email` alongside
`colaboratory`. Your existing token works with no extra sign-in.

``` python
acct = os.environ['FASTCOLAB_ACCOUNT']
c = await Colab.connect(account=acct, drive=False)
u0 = await c.usage()
assert u0.balance >= 0
u0
```

## Opening a live runtime in the browser

Runtimes from `v1beta.runtimes` have `r-...` IDs. Colab’s web UI expects
the shorter `/tun/m/` backend ID (`m-...`). `endpoint` decodes that ID
from the `aud` claim inside `rt.token`’s JWT payload (falling back to
the proxy hostname) with no extra request. `browser_url` builds a link
with both `?dbu=` and the unencoded `#datalabBackendUrl=` fragment.
Opening it attaches your browser directly to the running virtual
machine.

Start a High-RAM CPU runtime to exercise the rest of this notebook.
Calling `usage()` again shows the active assignment count and hourly
burn rate update right away.

``` python
rt = await c.start('cpu')
u1 = await c.usage()
assert u1.assignments_count >= u0.assignments_count
assert rt.endpoint.startswith('m-')
link = rt.browser_url()
assert f'/tun/m/{rt.endpoint}' in link and '#datalabBackendUrl=' in link
dict(endpoint=rt.endpoint, rate_hourly=u1.rate_hourly, active=u1.assignments_count, url=link)
```

## Connecting over SSH

Colab runtimes accept native SSH over `wss://{host}/colab/ssh` through
`jupyasyncclient`’s `jac-ssh --proxy` `ProxyCommand`.
[`colab_ssh`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/fastcolab/extras.html#colab_ssh)
saves a `fastcolab` runtime’s WebSocket URL, headers, and metadata in
`jupyasyncclient.ssh`’s session store
(`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/jupyasyncclient/ssh.json`) and appends a `Host` block
to `~/.ssh/config` when missing (or updates it with `replace=True`).
Plain `ssh`, `scp`, `rsync`, and Remote-SSH then work directly with no
`google-colab-cli` dependency. Colab rejects RSA keys; `jac-ssh` picks
`~/.ssh/id_ed25519` or `~/.ssh/id_ecdsa` automatically.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/fastcolab/blob/main/fastcolab/extras.py#L117"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

Check idempotency on a temporary SSH config, then register `rt` with
`rt.ssh()` and verify the stored session matches `rt.endpoint`.

``` python
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='fastcolab-ssh-') as td:
    tmp_cfg = Path(td)/'config'
    test_eq(colab_ssh(ssh_config=tmp_cfg), 'ssh colab')
    first = tmp_cfg.read_text()
    assert 'Host colab' in first and 'ProxyCommand ' in first
    colab_ssh(ssh_config=tmp_cfg)
    test_eq(tmp_cfg.read_text(), first)
```

``` python
cmd = rt.ssh()
sess = get_ssh_session('colab')
test_eq(cmd, 'ssh colab')
test_eq(sess.endpoint, rt.endpoint)
dict(cmd=cmd, endpoint=sess.endpoint)
```

## Shell commands and hardware inspection

Running shell commands directly through `rt.exec` means repeating
`subprocess.run` boilerplate every time. `sh` wraps that call behind a
unique JSON marker so shell output stays separate from kernel noise. It
returns `AttrDict(returncode, stdout, stderr)` and raises `RuntimeError`
on non-zero exits when `check=True`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/fastcolab/blob/main/fastcolab/extras.py#L134"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### ColabRuntime.sh

``` python
async def sh(
    cmd:str | list, # Shell command string (`shell=True`) or argv list (`shell=False`)
    cwd:str=None, # Working directory on the runtime
    env:dict=None, # Extra environment variables merged with the runtime environment
    check:bool=True, # Raise `RuntimeError` when the command exits non-zero?
    timeout:float=None, # Execution timeout in seconds
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Run a shell command on the runtime and return
`AttrDict(returncode, stdout, stderr)`.*

Verify `sh` with a string command, an argv list, and `check=False` on a
non-zero exit code:

``` python
r_ok = await rt.sh('uname -sr && which uv')
assert r_ok.returncode == 0 and 'Linux' in r_ok.stdout
r_fail = await rt.sh(['false'], check=False)
test_eq(r_fail.returncode, 1)
r_ok.stdout.strip()
```

Colab does not publish guaranteed RAM or disk quotas, and hardware
varies by region. `sys_info` queries the live machine in one call for
Python version, CPU count, RAM, `/content` disk space, GPUs
(`nvidia-smi`), and TPU settings.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/fastcolab/blob/main/fastcolab/extras.py#L155"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
async def sys_info()->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Return live Python, CPU, RAM, disk, GPU, and TPU details for this
runtime.*

``` python
info = await rt.sys_info()
assert info.cpus >= 2 and info.ram_gb > 10 and info.disk_gb > 20
info
```

## Syncing directories

Uploading a directory tree file by file over `/api/contents` requires
one HTTP request per directory and file. `upload_dir` packs the local
directory into one `.tar.gz` archive, uploads it with `rt.upload`
(reusing `00_core`’s 32 MB chunking), and extracts it remotely.
`DEFAULT_EXCLUDES` skips Git metadata, virtual environments, caches, and
`.DS_Store` files.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/fastcolab/blob/main/fastcolab/extras.py#L199"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### ColabRuntime.upload_dir

``` python
async def upload_dir(
    local_dir:str | pathlib.Path, # Local directory to archive and upload
    remote_dir:str='/content/work', # Destination directory on the runtime
    exclude:tuple=('.git', '__pycache__', '.venv', '.ipynb_checkpoints', 'node_modules', '.DS_Store', '*.pyc'), # Basename or glob patterns to skip
    clear:bool=False, # Remove existing contents of `remote_dir` before extracting?
    timeout:float=300, # Extraction timeout in seconds
)->str:
```

*Archive `local_dir` into a `.tar.gz`, upload it once, and extract it
into `remote_dir`.*

`download_dir` runs the reverse. It archives `remote_dir` into `/tmp`,
fetches it via `rt.download`, and removes the remote archive. Local
extraction uses `filter='data'` to keep paths inside `local_dir`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/fastcolab/blob/main/fastcolab/extras.py#L227"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### ColabRuntime.download_dir

``` python
async def download_dir(
    remote_dir:str, # Directory on the runtime to archive and download
    local_dir:str | pathlib.Path, # Local destination directory
    exclude:tuple=('.git', '__pycache__', '.venv', '.ipynb_checkpoints', 'node_modules', '.DS_Store', '*.pyc'), # Basename or glob patterns to skip
    timeout:float=300, # Archiving timeout in seconds
)->pathlib.Path:
```

*Archive `remote_dir` on the runtime, download it once, and unpack into
`local_dir`.*

Upload a nested local directory that also holds an ignored `__pycache__`
file. Then write a new file remotely and download the directory back
locally.

``` python
td = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='fastcolab-sync-')
src, dst = Path(td.name)/'src', Path(td.name)/'dst'
(src/'sub').mkdir(parents=True)
(src/'sub'/'hello.txt').write_text('hello from mac')
(src/'__pycache__').mkdir()
(src/'__pycache__'/'skip.pyc').write_bytes(b'ignore')
await rt.upload_dir(src, '/content/sync_demo', clear=True)
(await rt.sh('find /content/sync_demo -type f | sort')).stdout.strip()
```

``` python
await rt.sh(['python3', '-c', "open('/content/sync_demo/result.txt', 'w').write('computed on colab')"])
await rt.download_dir('/content/sync_demo', dst)
test_eq((dst/'sub'/'hello.txt').read_text(), 'hello from mac')
test_eq((dst/'result.txt').read_text(), 'computed on colab')
assert not (dst/'__pycache__').exists()
synced = sorted(p.relative_to(dst).as_posix() for p in dst.rglob('*') if p.is_file())
td.cleanup()
synced
```

## Running local scripts and notebooks remotely

Running a local `.py` file on a Colab kernel needs four small
adjustments.
[`_script_payload`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/fastcolab/extras.html#_script_payload)
strips any `#!` shebang, sets `__file__` and `sys.argv`, applies
temporary `os.environ` values before restoring them, and treats
`SystemExit(0)` as a clean exit rather than a traceback.
[`ColabRuntime.run_script`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/fastcolab/extras.html#colabruntime.run_script)
parses the exit marker and raises on non-zero exits when `check=True`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/fastcolab/blob/main/fastcolab/extras.py#L291"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### ColabRuntime.run_script

``` python
async def run_script(
    script:str | pathlib.Path, # Local path to a Python script
    args:list=None, # Command-line arguments exposed as `sys.argv[1:]`
    env:dict=None, # Temporary environment variables for the script
    check:bool=True, # Raise `RuntimeError` on unhandled exception or non-zero `SystemExit`?
    timeout:float=None, # Execution timeout in seconds
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Run a local Python script on this runtime and return
`AttrDict(returncode, text, outputs)`.*

Run a local script that starts with a shebang, reads `sys.argv` and an
environment variable, and exits explicitly via `sys.exit(0)`:

``` python
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='fastcolab-script-') as td:
    sp = Path(td)/'calc.py'
    sp.write_text('#!/usr/bin/env python3\nimport os, sys\nprint(int(sys.argv[1]) * int(os.environ["MULT"]))\nsys.exit(0)\n')
    sr = await rt.run_script(sp, args=['7'], env={'MULT': '6'})
test_eq(sr.returncode, 0)
test_eq(sr.text.strip(), '42')
sr
```

`run_nb` opens a fresh remote kernel and executes each code cell of a
local notebook in order. It writes the real Jupyter outputs back onto
every cell, shuts down the temporary kernel on exit, and optionally
saves the result to `out_path`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/fastcolab/blob/main/fastcolab/extras.py#L319"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### ColabRuntime.run_nb

``` python
async def run_nb(
    nb_path:str | pathlib.Path, # Local `.ipynb` path to execute remotely
    out_path:str | pathlib.Path=None, # Optional output `.ipynb` path (can match `nb_path` to save in place)
    allow_errors:bool=False, # Continue running later cells after a cell raises?
    timeout:float=None, # Per-cell execution timeout in seconds
)->fastcore.nbio.Notebook:
```

*Execute a local notebook on a fresh remote kernel, storing outputs on
each code cell.*

Create a two-cell notebook locally and run it on `rt`. Inspect the saved
output:

``` python
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='fastcolab-nb-') as td:
    inp, outp = Path(td)/'in.ipynb', Path(td)/'out.ipynb'
    write_nb(new_nb([mk_cell('x = 21'), mk_cell('x * 2')]), inp)
    executed = await rt.run_nb(inp, out_path=outp)
    saved = read_nb(outp)
    res_txt = outs_text(saved.cells[1].outputs).strip()
test_eq(res_txt, '42')
res_txt
```

[`Colab.run_script`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/fastcolab/extras.html#colab.run_script)
matches `colab run`. It provisions a runtime, uploads optional files or
directories, executes the script, and downloads requested artifacts. A
`finally` block deletes the runtime unless `keep=True`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/fastcolab/blob/main/fastcolab/extras.py#L342"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Colab.run_script

``` python
async def run_script(
    script:str | pathlib.Path, # Local path to a Python script
    hw:str | dict='cpu', # Hardware alias or raw `runtimeSpec` dict
    high_mem:bool=True, # Request `SHAPE_HIGHMEM` when supported?
    args:list=None, # Command-line arguments exposed as `sys.argv[1:]`
    env:dict=None, # Temporary environment variables for the script
    upload:dict=None, # Mapping `{local_path: remote_path}` of files or directories to upload first
    download:dict=None, # Mapping `{remote_path: local_path}` of files or directories to download after
    keep:bool=False, # Keep the runtime alive after finishing instead of deleting it?
    check:bool=True, # Raise `RuntimeError` on non-zero exit?
    timeout:float=None, # Execution timeout in seconds
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*Provision a runtime, run a local script with optional uploads and
artifact downloads, and clean up.*

Run an ephemeral job on a fresh CPU runtime. This uploads `in.txt`,
transforms it remotely, downloads `out.txt`, and deletes the runtime on
exit.

``` python
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='fastcolab-run-') as td:
    td = Path(td)
    (td/'in.txt').write_text('fastcolab')
    sp = td/'job.py'
    sp.write_text("from pathlib import Path\nPath('/content/out.txt').write_text(Path('/content/in.txt').read_text().upper())\nprint('done')\n")
    ephem = await c.run_script(sp, hw='cpu', upload={td/'in.txt': '/content/in.txt'}, download={'/content/out.txt': td/'out.txt'})
    artifact = (td/'out.txt').read_text()
test_eq(ephem.returncode, 0)
test_eq(artifact, 'FASTCOLAB')
dict(text=ephem.text, artifact=artifact)
```

## Cleaning up runtimes

`stop_all` deletes active runtimes on your account in one call. Pass
`ids` to target specific runtimes, or `dry_run=True` to preview what
would stop without deleting anything.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/fastcolab/blob/main/fastcolab/extras.py#L373"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Colab.stop_all

``` python
async def stop_all(
    ids:list=None, # Optional subset of runtime IDs or resource names to delete (`None` means all)
    dry_run:bool=False, # Return matched runtime IDs without deleting them?
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
```

*Delete active Colab runtimes on this account and return the matched
runtime IDs.*

Preview `stop_all` with `dry_run=True`. Then delete only this notebook’s
runtime (`rt`) and verify it is gone.

``` python
matched = await c.stop_all(ids=[rt.id], dry_run=True)
test_eq(list(matched), [rt.id])
stopped = await c.stop_all(ids=[rt.id])
test_eq(list(stopped), [rt.id])
remaining = await c.runtimes()
assert all(r.id != rt.id for r in remaining)
remove_ssh_session('colab')
stopped
```
